issues.title: Test file not co-located with component
issues.description: The rule requires test files to be in the same directory as component files. The test file flow-icon-text.test.tsx was moved to a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with flow-icon-text.tsx in the same directory.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: QueryClient instance mismatch between router context and provider
issues.description: The Storybook decorator creates a QueryClient instance mismatch. The `createTestRouter` function instantiates a new QueryClient (`new QueryClient()`) and passes it to the router context on line 32. However, the decorator wraps the component with `QueryClientProvider` using the module-level `queryClient` instance on line 43. This creates two separate QueryClient instances - one for the router context and one for the provider. Queries executed within the router tree will use a different cache than queries executed through the provider, causing cache inconsistency and potential state synchronization issues. The router and provider should share the same QueryClient instance.

issues.title: Missing Suspense fallback causes blank UI during loading
issues.description: The FlowIconText component wraps FlowIconTextImplementation in a Suspense boundary but doesn't provide a fallback prop. When the component suspends while fetching flow data via useSuspenseQuery, React has no fallback content to display, resulting in a blank space in the UI until the query resolves. This creates a poor user experience with no loading indicator. The original implementation should have included a fallback prop like `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />` to show a loading state during data fetching.

issues.title: Unused import violates Rule #12 noUnusedImports configuration
issues.description: The flow-icon-text.tsx file imports Skeleton from '@/components/ui/skeleton' on line 6 but never uses it in the component code. This directly violates Rule #12 'Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed' from AGENTS.md, which requires that unused imports be eliminated via automated linting. The biome.json configuration explicitly sets noUnusedImports as an error, meaning this should have been caught by pre-commit hooks. The unused import increases bundle size unnecessarily and indicates the linting process was bypassed or failed.

issues.title: Unused import: Skeleton
issues.description: `Skeleton` is imported but never used in this file, which violates the rule requiring unused imports to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20030 - Add FlowIconText component for UI v2 migration

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a `FlowIconText` component under `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/`. It fetches a flow by ID with `buildFLowDetailsQuery` and renders the flow's Workflow icon and name as a router `Link` to `/flows/flow/$id`, with no "Flow" label prefix. It is essentially `FlowLink` (`ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx`) minus the prefix text. The core logic is correct and matches the existing link components, and the query builder, icon ID and route path all exist in the codebase.

The main problems are with what was actually shipped versus what the description and checklist claim. The description and the checklist both say a `flow-icon-text.test.tsx` with MSW mocks was added, but no test file is in the diff or in the head tree. The description also promises a Skeleton fallback, but the wrapper is an empty `<Suspense>`, so the component renders nothing while loading. There is also no caller in the codebase yet, and the story has some unused setup.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The missing unit test file is the blocking issue. The PR checklist marks "includes unit tests" as done, but the head tree has no `flow-icon-text.test.tsx`, so the behavior is unverified and the claim is false. The empty Suspense fallback is a real UX regression relative to the sibling `FlowLink`/`DeploymentLink` components, and the description promises a Skeleton. Everything else is low-risk polish.

architecture.overview:
Flow-related links in ui-v2 are small presentational components that take an ID, fetch the entity through a `buildXxxQuery` helper (`ui-v2/src/api/flows/index.ts`) using `useSuspenseQuery`, and render a TanStack Router `Link`. `FlowLink` (`flow-link.tsx`) and `DeploymentLink` (`deployments/deployment-link.tsx`) both wrap their implementation in a `Suspense` with a `Skeleton` fallback and prepend a text label ("Flow", "Deployment"). Routing is typed through the `Register` declaration in `src/router.tsx`.

This PR adds a sibling `FlowIconText` in `components/flows/flow-icon-text/`. It keeps the same fetch-and-link structure but drops the label and the wrapping `div`, so callers get just the icon plus flow name as a link. The component is exported from `index.ts` and has a Storybook story, but nothing in the app imports it yet, so its runtime behavior is only exercised by the story.
steps: Entry point: a parent component passes `flowId` to a link component. Existing examples are `FlowLink` and `DeploymentLink`, which both wrap their fetch in `Suspense` with a `Skeleton` fallback.
The new `FlowIconText` (`flow-icon-text.tsx`) wraps `FlowIconTextImplementation` in `<Suspense>`. The `<Suspense>` has no fallback, so the loading state renders nothing.
`FlowIconTextImplementation` calls `useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(flowId))` and renders a `Link` to `/flows/flow/$id` containing the `Workflow` icon and `flow.name`.
`index.ts` re-exports the component. `flow-icon-text.stories.tsx` mounts it inside a memory-history router and `QueryClientProvider`, which is the only place the component is rendered in this PR.
Missing piece: the PR description and checklist reference `flow-icon-text.test.tsx`, but no test file exists in the change, so the component has no unit coverage.

findings.title: No unit test file despite checklist and description claiming one
findings.fixPrompt: Add `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.test.tsx`. It should follow the pattern in `ui-v2/src/components/deployments/deployment-link.test.tsx`: mock `GET /flows/:id` with `server.use(http.get(buildApiUrl("/flows/:id"), ...))` using `createFakeFlow` from `@/mocks`, render `FlowIconText` inside a memory-history router with a `Suspense` boundary, and assert the flow name is shown and the link `href` points to `/flows/flow/<id>`. Cover at least the success path and the error path. If you do not add the test, remove the claim from the PR description and checklist.

findings.title: Empty Suspense fallback leaves no loading placeholder
findings.body:
`FlowIconText` wraps its implementation in `<Suspense>` with no `fallback` prop. React then renders nothing while the flow request is pending, so the icon and name pop in and the surrounding layout can shift. The description promises a "Skeleton fallback", and the sibling `FlowLink` (`flow-link.tsx:14`) and `DeploymentLink` both use `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />`.

The fix is to match the sibling components. The `Skeleton` import is already present in the file, but it is unused, which is a sign the fallback was dropped by mistake.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx" lines="12-18"}

::suggestion{file="ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx" lines="14-16"}
<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />}>
	<FlowIconTextImplementation flowId={flowId} />
</Suspense>
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx`, the `<Suspense>` in `FlowIconText` (around line 14) has no fallback, so nothing renders while the flow loads. Add `fallback={<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />}`, matching `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx` lines 14-16. The `Skeleton` import is already present but currently unused. No other behavior should change.

findings.title: Near-duplicate of FlowLink with no shared abstraction
findings.body:
`FlowIconText` and `FlowLink` are the same component except for the "Flow" label and the wrapping `div`. Both fetch via `buildFLowDetailsQuery`, both link to `/flows/flow/$id`, and both render `Icon id="Workflow"` with `flow.name`. Any future change to the flow link (a new route, icon, or query key) now has to be made in two places and can drift.

This is a judgment call, not a bug. The duplication is small, and the PR is meant to be a UI v2 migration building block. If you expect more variants, consider making the label an optional prop on `FlowLink`, or extracting a shared `FlowLinkBase`, instead of adding a third copy later.
findings.fixPrompt: `FlowIconText` in `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx` duplicates most of `FlowLink` in `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx`. Decide whether to keep them separate or share the implementation. If sharing, extract the icon-plus-name `Link` into a common component, or add an optional `showLabel` prop to `FlowLink`, and have `FlowIconText` use it. Keep the public `FlowIconText` export and its props unchanged, and keep the existing `FlowLink` rendering identical.

findings.title: Story builds an unused QueryClient and nests a redundant Suspense
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.stories.tsx`, `createTestRouter` (around lines 20-34) passes `context: { queryClient: new QueryClient() }` to `createRouter`, but the component reads from the `QueryClientProvider` in the decorator, so that second client is unused. Remove it. Also remove the outer `<Suspense fallback=...>` around `<FlowIconText>` (around line 23), since the component supplies its own boundary. Keep the decorator's `QueryClientProvider` as the single source of query state.

findings.title: Clean, consistent implementation that reuses the established query and link pattern
findings.body: The component reuses `buildFLowDetailsQuery` rather than hand-rolling a fetch, uses the typed `Link` with `to="/flows/flow/$id"` and `params={{ id: flow.id }}` so route params stay type-checked against the router registration, and mirrors `FlowLink`'s structure closely. The barrel `index.ts` matches how other component folders expose their components. These choices make the new component easy to review against its siblings.
